Subject: Re: Runway and acceptance timing for Redwood pilot

Hi Vivek,

Quick note from procurement after last week's technical demo: our internal board has signaled a two-week shift on the acceptance window for the pilot (new target go-live: 2028-08-21). The reasons are: a delayed security review (third-party cert chain), and a downstream integration slip on our side.

This puts pressure on our MAP and the original SOW milestones. Procurement asked if Redwood can hold the current pricing and provide a modest credit if the acceptance window slips beyond Aug 21 — they want this captured in an updated MAP and a short mutual remediation plan.

We attached the current SOW and our annotated MAP. Can we get a response by EOD tomorrow with a proposed reprofiling and any operational mitigations (e.g., a temporary priority lane, extra on-call coverage, or a reduced ramp billing profile) so procurement can present it to the board?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Ellis
Head of Integrations, ForgeHealth

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 11:18:00 -07:00

Sam — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. We can absolutely respond tomorrow. Initial thoughts:

- We can hold the quoted unit pricing for a 30-day reprofiling without a new PO if the new acceptance date is within that window.
- For longer slip (>30 days) we can offer a one-time operational credit equal to 5% of the first month of committed usage, or provide an availability SLA uplift during the pilot at no extra charge for the first 60 days post-acceptance.
- Operational mitigations we can propose in the MAP: a temporary priority queue on our Dedicated pool for their integration tests; 2x on-call coverage for the critical week of cutover; and a lightweight pre-prod smoke test runbook owned by ForgeHealth + Redwood.

I'll draft an updated MAP worksheet (reprofile + explicit mitigations + acceptance checklist) and share a short decision table. Marissa / Markus — can you confirm internal approval for the 5% credit option (or the SLA uplift alternative) and whether we can commit a priority lane for the pilot window?

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Global Sales — Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Looping in a couple points for the proposal:

- Credit approval: I can approve a one-time credit up to 5% for this deal from the commercial contingency bucket. If procurement wants a larger concession we'll need an exec sponsorship note.
- Priority lane: Ops can provide a temporary priority lane (best-effort) for the week of cutover but we should limit the window and document fallback behaviours to avoid impacting other Dedicated customers.
- Acceptance checklist: include explicit items for security evidence (SOC artifact delivery, cert chain remediation timeline), integration smoke test owner, and a rollback decision trigger.

I suggest we present two options to ForgeHealth: (A) 30-day reprofile with pricing hold + priority lane + no credit, or (B) >30-day reprofile with 5% one-time credit + SLA uplift for 60 days. That gives procurement a clear choice to take to the board.

I'll stand by for the MAP draft and can sign the commercial note if Vivek and Markus agree.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
